S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific Phobia is characterized by a persistent, excessive fear of a clearly circumscribed object or situation (e.g., animals, heights, flying, injections) that is out of proportion to the actual danger and has lasted at least six months. The feared object or situation is consistently avoided or endured with marked distress, and this pattern leads to significant interference in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. Onset is often in childhood or adolescence, but clinically significant impairment may not emerge or be recognized until later life when demands change (e.g., job travel, caregiving, environmental shifts). It is distinguished from broader anxiety disorders by its narrow, specific trigger and from trauma‑related conditions by the absence of a pervasive trauma response beyond the circumscribed phobic context.

patient.stressor: Two years ago, Lindell was assigned to a new commercial account at an older office building where she accidentally spilled a highly concentrated industrial cleaning agent; the fumes overwhelmed her, and she had to be taken to the emergency room by EMTs, an experience that left her shaken even though she recovered physically. Before that incident, she had taken pride in her comfort around all kinds of cleaning supplies and even collected unusual products, but afterward she began reorganizing her routes to avoid certain storage closets and delegating any task that involved stronger chemicals to coworkers when possible. Her supervisors initially accommodated her requests, but as contracts changed she was expected to handle more specialized products again, and she found herself turning down better-paying assignments and working fewer hours to avoid those environments. When a new supervisor warned that continued refusal to work with standard chemicals could jeopardize her job, and she noticed she was even avoiding using some basic cleaners at home, she agreed to see a psychiatrist at the urging of a union representative who was concerned about how much this specific fear was limiting her work options.
patient.chief_complaint: “Any time I have to deal with those stronger cleaning chemicals, I either go out of my way to avoid them or push through it while feeling like I can’t stand being there.”

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: Ever since that day with the spill, just seeing a big drum or jug with a hazard symbol on it makes my stomach drop and I feel this wave of fear, even if everyone tells me it’s just a regular cleaner we’ve used for years with no problem.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: If I even think I might have to open a supply closet with the stronger stuff, my heart starts pounding, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t get a full breath before I’ve even touched the door handle, and it gets ten times worse the second I smell any kind of chemical smell.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: At work now I’ll walk the long way around the building to avoid certain closets, swap tasks with coworkers, or call in sick if I know those heavy-duty products are on the schedule, and on the rare times I can’t get out of it I stand there shaking, holding my breath and rushing through the job while feeling like I’m about to pass out or bolt out the door.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because of this fear, I’ve turned down higher-paying routes, cut back my hours, and come close to being written up since I keep refusing jobs that involve the standard chemicals everyone else handles without a second thought.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on ever since that spill at the new building, so it’s been about two years now.
